expansionPanelsText.expansionPanelsTitle: Benefits and harms of breast cancer screening:
expansionPanelsText.chancePreventTitle: Chance of preventing breast cancer death
expansionPanelsText.chancePreventText: Screening may prevent breast cancer death.
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveDef1: In breast cancer screening, a false positive means that the first test (mammogram) is “positive” (meaning that there is a signal of a possible cancer) but further tests don’t confirm breast cancer. Further tests include biopsies, which are surgeries where tissue is removed from the body for testing.
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveDef2: When people get a false positive, they aren’t diagnosed with breast cancer after all.
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveConsequencesTitle: What can happen when people get a false positive
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveCons1: Waiting for the results of further tests, not knowing if breast cancer will be diagnosed or not, can cause stress and anxiety.
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveCons2: People get tests they didn’t need to have (for example, biopsies).
expansionPanelsText.falsePositiveCons3: Biopsies may cause complications such as infections or bleeding.
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisIntro: In breast cancer screening, overdiagnosis happens when breast cancer is diagnosed by healthcare professionals but the cancer is:
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisItem1: indolent (meaning it will not cause pain or harm),
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisItem2: non-progressive (meaning it will not grow or get worse),
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisItem3: not deadly (meaning it will not cause death)
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisEnding: and when breast cancer treatments (for example, surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, or other treatments) have a low chance of helping the person.
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisConsequencesTitle: What can happen when people are overdiagnosed
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisConsIntro: Being labeled as a “cancer patient” can change how people feel and choices they make.
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsIntro: Breast cancer tests and treatments can:
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsItem1: cause side effects (for example, surgery may cause pain and need recovery time)
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsItem3: be a hassle (for example, going to a lot of appointments)
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsItem4: cost people money (for example, parking costs, time unable to work)
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsItem5: cost the health care system money and resources (for example, doctors’ time)
expansionPanelsText.overdiagnosisTestsItem6: contribute to the “overmedicalization” of society (that is, turning too many things into medical problems)
